social.title: Guinguette Night at Chez Gégène
social.description: On the Marne at Joinville, this century-old guinguette still does what it's always done — accordion, dancing between courses, and carafes of wine on checked tablecloths until nobody remembers being a stranger.
social.bonus: Dance at least once with someone you didn't arrive with.

social.title: Late-night Pigalle bar crawl
social.description: Pigalle SoPi (South Pigalle) is the most genuinely fun nightlife district in Paris — cramped bars, good music, late kitchens, and nobody going home before 2am.
social.bonus: Visit at least five bars. Order the house thing at each one.

social.title: Jazz at New Morning, Rue des Petites-Écuries
social.description: The bare-brick hall on Rue des Petites-Écuries has hosted Chet Baker, Prince, and every serious jazz act passing through Paris since 1981 — check the bill, buy the ticket, stand close.
social.bonus: Get to the front. Stand close to the music.

social.title: Cocktails at Terrass Hotel rooftop, Montmartre
social.description: Montmartre's rooftop bars at sunset — Sacré-Cœur glowing above and all of Paris below — are one of the great city-view experiences in the world.
social.bonus: Stay for the second cocktail. The light is better by then.

social.title: Sunday Afternoon at Rosa Bonheur
social.description: Rosa Bonheur in the Parc des Buttes-Chaumont is Paris's best outdoor guinguette — a boules pitch, a bar, and 500 Parisians all in one green hillside clearing.
social.bonus: Challenge a strangers' pétanque team to a game — loser buys a round.

social.title: Cocktails at Le Syndicat
social.description: Le Syndicat on Rue du Faubourg Saint-Denis is a militant French spirits bar — every bottle on the back shelf is French, the cocktails are original, and the crowd knows exactly where they are.
social.bonus: Order whatever the bartender is personally drinking tonight — then actually finish it.

social.title: Late Night at Le Caveau de la Huchette
social.description: This jazz and swing club in a medieval Latin Quarter cellar has been running continuous sessions since 1946 — the dance floor fills up and stays full until 2am.
social.bonus: Ask a stranger to dance during the first song — no experience required, no excuses accepted.

social.title: Aperitivo on Canal Saint-Martin
social.description: The iron footbridges and tree-lined banks of Canal Saint-Martin are where the 10th arrondissement spills outside every evening with wine, snacks, and nowhere to be.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with the group next to you — in French — and get at least one local restaurant recommendation out of it.

adventure.title: Boulder the Fontainebleau Forest
adventure.description: The birthplace of modern bouldering is forty minutes from Gare de Lyon — rent a crash pad, follow the painted circuit arrows through the pines at Bas Cuvier, and climb where every legend learned.
adventure.bonus: Complete one full colored circuit — even the kids' one counts if you finish every problem.

adventure.title: Climb the Arc de Triomphe at Dusk
adventure.description: Two hundred and eighty-four spiral steps put you dead center of the twelve avenues as they light up — the only rooftop in Paris where the Eiffel Tower sparkles on the hour just for you.
adventure.bonus: Stay for the top of the hour — count the avenues out loud while the tower glitters.

adventure.title: Trail Run Through the Bois de Vincennes
adventure.description: Paris's largest park serves up 995 hectares of actual forest trails, lake paths, and zero tourists — the eastern loop past Lac Daumesnil is genuinely wild feeling.
adventure.bonus: Run the full perimeter of Lac Daumesnil without stopping — it's 3.5km and the path is uneven enough to keep you honest.

adventure.title: Outdoor Workout at Fitness Stations, Berges de Seine
adventure.description: The Left Bank riverbanks between Pont d'Iéna and Pont de l'Alma host a full outdoor gym where Parisians grind through calisthenics with the Eiffel Tower looming directly overhead.
adventure.bonus: Do 10 pull-ups at the bars closest to the Eiffel Tower — with the tower in your eyeline the entire time.

adventure.title: Dawn Balloon Flight from Fontainebleau
adventure.description: Lift off at first light with the operators who've flown the Fontainebleau forest for decades — château, treetops, and the Île-de-France unrolling in complete silence before the region wakes.
adventure.bonus: Keep your eyes open during the burner blast directly above your head — no looking away.

adventure.title: Wander the Palais Garnier
adventure.description: The grand staircase, the Chagall ceiling, and the velvet-red auditorium of Paris's opera house — take the self-guided visit and find the box Leroux gave to the Phantom.
adventure.bonus: Find the bronze bust of composer Hector Berlioz and take a photo making the same expression as the sculpture.

adventure.title: Paddle the Bassin de la Villette
adventure.description: The municipal base nautique at La Villette puts you in a kayak on Paris's widest water — street art, barges, and the raw northeastern edge of the city gliding past at water level.
adventure.bonus: Paddle all the way to the Parc de la Villette basin without stopping — buy a coffee from the floating café when you arrive.

adventure.title: Night run along the Seine
adventure.description: Paris at night on the quays — lamplit bridges, empty roads, the Eiffel Tower sparkling on the hour — is the best run in any city in the world.
adventure.bonus: Run from Trocadéro to Notre-Dame without stopping.

adventure.title: Morning run along the Seine riverbanks
adventure.description: The Berges de Seine, car-free since 2013, is 4.5km of riverside path from Pont de l'Alma to Pont de Sully — morning light, almost no one, cafes just opening.
adventure.bonus: Start at the Eiffel Tower. Finish at Notre-Dame. Non-negotiable.

adventure.title: Rooftop drinks at Le Perchoir Ménilmontant
adventure.description: Seven floors above the 11th, Le Perchoir's original rooftop pours cocktails with a 360° sweep from Sacré-Cœur to the Eiffel Tower — arrive before golden hour or expect the queue.
adventure.bonus: Tell no one where it is. Earn it.

adventure.title: SUP on the Marne river
adventure.description: The Marne east of Paris has calm water, guinguettes on the banks, and SUP rental operators — an afternoon on the water feels nothing like being in a capital city.
adventure.bonus: Paddle to a guinguette and eat lunch on the board.

adventure.title: Vélib cycle across all 20 arrondissements
adventure.description: Paris is technically compact enough to cycle end-to-end in two hours on a Vélib — route yourself through all 20 arrondissements and touch a landmark in each.
adventure.bonus: Find one thing in an arrondissement you'd never visited before.

adventure.title: Walk the Coulée Verte from Bastille to Vincennes
adventure.description: The elevated Coulée Verte René-Dumont — the 1993 planted walkway that inspired New York's High Line — runs 4.5km from Bastille toward the Bois de Vincennes at treetop level.
adventure.bonus: Go the full 4.5km end to end without stopping.

adventure.title: Pétanque in the Jardins du Palais Royal
adventure.description: The graveled gardens behind the Louvre are where Parisians play pétanque under the arcades — join a game, lose gracefully, and stay for another round.
adventure.bonus: Challenge the winners to a rematch.

adventure.title: Catacombs tour after dark (guided)
adventure.description: Six million Parisians are stacked in 300km of tunnels under your feet — a guided evening tour of the ossuary goes further than the public entrance and turns something grim into something genuinely astonishing.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full distance without any light except the guide's.

adventure.title: Climb at Block'Out bouldering gym
adventure.description: Paris bouldering is quietly serious — Block'Out Saint-Ouen, just past the Périphérique, sets 1,200m² of modern problems weekly and keeps a terrace for recovery beers.
adventure.bonus: Finish a problem one grade harder than your usual. Ask for a beta if you're stuck.

adventure.title: Swim at the Piscine Joséphine Baker on the Seine
adventure.description: Paris's floating outdoor pool is moored on the Seine with a retractable glass roof — lap swimming on a river in the center of Paris is genuinely unusual.
adventure.bonus: Do 30 laps then sit on the deck above the river and stare at the city.

adventure.title: Nordic walk through the Bois de Boulogne
adventure.description: The 846-hectare forest west of Paris has 37km of trails — rent poles at the gatehouse and do a full Nordic walk through to the Longchamp racecourse.
adventure.bonus: Find the waterfall garden inside the forest. It's easy to miss.

adventure.title: Cycle to Versailles on La Véloscénie
adventure.description: The first leg of La Véloscénie greenway links Paris to Versailles on mostly traffic-free paths through the Meudon woods — a half-day out-and-back ending at the palace gates.
adventure.bonus: Eat your lunch on the palace grounds. Bike it back before dark.

adventure.title: Skate the Trocadéro Esplanade
adventure.description: The marble esplanade in front of the Trocadéro with the Eiffel Tower dead ahead is where Paris's skate scene has held court for decades — bladers, skaters, and onlookers all day long.
adventure.bonus: Borrow a skater's board for one run across the esplanade — negotiate it yourself, no money involved.

adventure.title: Climb to the Summit of the Eiffel Tower on Foot
adventure.description: Taking the stairs to the second floor — and pushing on to the summit by lift — makes the Eiffel Tower a physical event, not a passive one.
adventure.bonus: Walk every single stair to the second floor (674 steps) without using the elevator — time yourself.

adventure.title: Run the Bois de Boulogne at Dawn
adventure.description: The 845-hectare Bois de Boulogne in the early morning belongs to runners and cyclists — the lakes catch the mist and the city hasn't woken up yet.
adventure.bonus: Loop the Lac Inférieur without stopping — roughly 3.5km — and log your time.

adventure.title: Climb the Towers of Notre-Dame de Paris
adventure.description: The north tower climb puts you face-to-face with the gargoyles and gives you a medieval vantage point that the cathedral floor never can.
adventure.bonus: Find Emmanuel the great bell and press your hand flat against the bronze — feel the history in the metal.

adventure.title: Night Vélib' Ride Along the Seine
adventure.description: Grab a Vélib' bike after 10pm and ride the riverside quais from Pont de l'Alma to Notre-Dame while the city glows and the tourists sleep.
adventure.bonus: Stop on Pont des Arts at midnight and yell something into the river — loud enough to echo.

adventure.title: Rooftop of Galeries Lafayette
adventure.description: The free rooftop terrace of Paris's most iconic department store hands you one of the best unobstructed views of the Haussmann skyline with zero ticket price.
adventure.bonus: Spot the Eiffel Tower, Sacré-Cœur, and the Pompidou from the same standing spot — snap them in one panoramic sweep.

chill.title: Sunday Morning at Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen
chill.description: The world's largest antiques market sprawls across Clignancourt with 2,500 dealers and the particular smell of old leather, silver, and very good coffee from the market stalls.
chill.bonus: Negotiate a dealer down by at least 20% on something you actually want to buy — no walking away until you've tried.

chill.title: Read in the Jardin du Luxembourg
chill.description: The metal chairs of the Luxembourg are a Paris institution — drag one to a sunny spot near the octagonal fountain, open a book, and don't move for two hours.
chill.bonus: Don't bring your phone inside the park. Leave it at the gate.

chill.title: Golden hour picnic on the Seine quays
chill.description: The lower quays along the Seine between Pont de l'Alma and Pont d'Iena fill at dusk with Paris's best informal picnic culture — join it with wine and something from a market.
chill.bonus: Stay until the Eiffel Tower sparkle display goes off.

chill.title: Espresso at Café Procope, Saint-Germain-des-Prés
chill.description: Café Procope has poured coffee since 1686 — Voltaire ran a tab here. Order a café crème, take the chair facing Rue de l'Ancienne Comédie, and don't look at your phone for an hour.
chill.bonus: Order a second café without being asked. Just raise your hand.

chill.title: Afternoon nap in the Tuileries garden chairs
chill.description: The Tuileries metal chairs are designed for lounging, positioned for people-watching, and available to drag wherever the sun is — the Louvre on one end, the Ferris wheel on the other.

chill.title: Wander the covered passages of the 2nd arrondissement
chill.description: The 19th-century glass-roofed galeries — Vivénne, Colbert, Véro-Dodat — are intact shopping arcades preserved like time capsules from another Paris.
chill.bonus: Count all the passages and rank them by atmosphere.

chill.title: Sunset from Sacré-Cœur Steps
chill.description: The west-facing steps of Sacré-Cœur at golden hour turn the entire Paris basin amber — bring something to drink and stay until the Eiffel Tower lights up.
chill.bonus: Don't pull out your phone for the first 10 minutes after sitting down — just watch the city change color.

chill.title: Wander Père Lachaise Cemetery
chill.description: Père Lachaise is the most beautiful urban cemetery in the world — 44 hectares of cobbled paths, crumbling mausoleums, and a cast of residents that reads like a syllabus.
chill.bonus: Find Jim Morrison's grave without using Google Maps — ask a groundskeeper or follow the handmade signs left by pilgrims.

chill.title: Afternoon Tea at Angélina
chill.description: The house hot chocolate at Angélina on Rue de Rivoli has been the thickest, most indulgent cup in Paris since 1903 — drink it slowly or not at all.
chill.bonus: Order the Mont-Blanc pastry alongside the hot chocolate and eat both in under 20 minutes — it's harder than it sounds.

chill.title: Afternoon at Jardin du Palais Royal
chill.description: The arcaded gardens of the Palais Royal are one of Paris's great secret courtyards — calm, beautiful, and completely off the tourist radar.
chill.bonus: Sit on the same bench for 30 minutes without touching your phone — count how many languages you hear pass by.

culture.title: Afternoon at Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature, Le Marais
culture.description: This gloriously strange hunting museum in a 17th-century Marais hôtel particulier blends taxidermy, Flemish masters, and contemporary art in rooms that feel like fever dreams.
culture.bonus: Find the secret room hidden behind a bookcase and photograph it before anyone else in your group notices it exists.

culture.title: Early morning at the Musée d'Orsay
culture.description: The Impressionist collection on the top floor at 9:31am, before any group tours arrive — you and the Monets in a converted train station with almost nobody else.
culture.bonus: Pick one painting to sit in front of for ten full minutes. Set a timer.

culture.title: Film at Le Grand Rex, Grands Boulevards
culture.description: The Grands Boulevards district has the most beautiful old movie palaces in Europe — find a showing at Le Grand Rex or Max Linder and see something with the lights all the way up.
culture.bonus: See something you know nothing about. Let the poster pick it.

culture.title: Street-art walk with a guide in Belleville
culture.description: Belleville is the nerve center of Paris street art — self-guided or with a Visite Atelier guide, the murals range from political to absurd to enormous.
culture.bonus: Find one you think is genuinely great and photograph only that one.

culture.title: Sunday reading afternoon at Shakespeare and Company
culture.description: The legendary English-language bookshop on the Left Bank runs Sunday afternoon readings in its cramped upper library — show up without knowing who's speaking.
culture.bonus: Buy one book you didn't come in for.

foodie.title: French onion soup at Au Pied de Cochon, Les Halles
foodie.description: Gratinated, dark, deeply savory — Paris onion soup at a late-night brasserie is one of the great cheap meals in any city in the world.
foodie.bonus: Order nothing else. Let it be dinner.

foodie.title: Croissant at Du Pain et des Idées, Canal Saint-Martin
foodie.description: Christophe Vasseur's 1889-vintage boulangerie near Canal Saint-Martin bakes the most argued-about croissant in Paris — go on a weekday morning, add a pain des amis, and eat both on the canal.
foodie.bonus: Eat all three before 9am. The decision must be made on the spot.

foodie.title: Natural wine at La Cave de Belleville
foodie.description: The Belleville cave à manger pours minimal-intervention wines by the glass with serious charcuterie boards — taste five things you've never heard of and be changed.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pick everything. No input from you.

foodie.title: Lunch at Frenchie, Rue du Nil, 2nd
foodie.description: Grégory Marchand's Rue du Nil flagship anchors Paris's bistronomie movement — serious cooking at lunch prices; book ahead and give the afternoon to it.
foodie.bonus: Ask the chef what they ate for staff meal. The answer is usually better.

foodie.title: Pâtisserie at Jacques Genin, Le Marais
foodie.description: Jacques Genin's Rue de Turenne salon is the Marais's most serious sweet stop — mango-passion caramels, sculptural fruit jellies, and a Paris-Brest assembled when you order it.
foodie.bonus: Rate each one out of 10 and keep a running score.

foodie.title: Steak-frites at Bistrot Paul Bert, 11th
foodie.description: The 11th arrondissement has a cluster of old-school zinc-bar bistros where steak-frites is still a serious act — sit at the bar and order it saignant.
foodie.bonus: Order the wine the waiter recommends, not the one you'd normally pick.

foodie.title: Tasting menu at Guy Savoy, Monnaie de Paris
foodie.description: Guy Savoy's dining room inside the Monnaie de Paris looks over the Seine — the artichoke and black truffle soup with brioche has anchored the menu for decades. Give the table the evening.
foodie.bonus: Describe the meal in writing before you sleep. The detail fades faster than you think.

foodie.title: Canal Saint-Martin picnic with market cheese and wine
foodie.description: Buy cheese from a fromagerie, wine from a cave, bread from a boulangerie, and eat all of it on the canal bank while bikes and barges pass.
foodie.bonus: Don't bring plates. Eat off the paper.

foodie.title: Ramen at Kodawari Ramen, Rue Monsieur-le-Prince
foodie.description: The original Kodawari counter on Rue Monsieur-le-Prince recreates a Tokyo yokocho down to the soundtrack — the line down the street knows exactly what it's waiting for.
foodie.bonus: Slurp loudly. This is the only appropriate response.

foodie.title: Crêpes at Breizh Café, Le Marais
foodie.description: Cancale butter, buckwheat galettes, and a proper Breton cider list — Breizh Café's Marais dining room is the standing argument that a crêpe is cuisine, not street food.
foodie.bonus: Order beurre sucre only. No Nutella. You're not a tourist.

foodie.title: Wine Bar at Le Verre Volé
foodie.description: This tiny canal-side cave à manger on Rue de Lancry has been the city's natural wine HQ since 2000 — small plates, great bottles, zero pretension.
foodie.bonus: Pick a bottle blind from the back shelf — price under €30 — and commit to finishing it without checking the label first.

foodie.title: Market Lunch at Marché d'Aligre
foodie.description: The Aligre market in the 12th is the most alive food market in Paris — cheap, loud, and stuffed with the best olives, charcuterie, and fresh bread in the city.
foodie.bonus: Build a full picnic lunch spending under €10 total — every item from a different stall.

foodie.title: Dinner at Septime
foodie.description: Bertrand Grébaut's neo-bistro in the 11th is the definitive argument that modern French cooking is the most exciting food in the world right now.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair a natural wine you've never heard of with your main — then finish the entire glass before Googling the domaine.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Café de Flore
foodie.description: The existentialists are gone but the buttery tartines, grand crème, and relentless people-watching on Boulevard Saint-Germain absolutely are not.
foodie.bonus: Order in French only — no English, no pointing — and hold eye contact with the waiter through the whole exchange.
